subject: general
question: Who among the following Governor Generals of India wrote about the predicament of Indian weavers, “The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck served as the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• He is known for his significant social reforms including the abolition of Sati.
 
• Bentinck highlighted the plight of Indian weavers due to British policies that favored British textiles over local products.
 
• His quote, "The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India," reflects the devastating impact of these policies on Indian textile workers.
 
• His tenure is often remembered for addressing the economic and social issues created by British colonial policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Revolution Impact:** The British Industrial Revolution led to the import of cheap British textiles, severely impacting Indian weavers.
 
• **Economic Policies:** British economic policies during colonial rule were aimed at benefiting British industries at the expense of Indian economy.
 
• **Sati Abolition:** One of the major social reforms under Bentinck was the abolition of the practice of Sati in 1829.
 
• **Education Reforms:** Bentinck also initiated reforms in the Indian education system, promoting English as the medium of instruction.
 
• **Judicial Reforms:** He made significant changes to the judicial system, including the introduction of jury trials and the appointment of Indians to higher judicial positions.
